content:
Following the release of the seventh developer beta for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and Apple's other upcoming software updates, Apple has now begun rolling out the corresponding public beta versions. Here are the details.

Apple Releases New Public Beta Versions

Apple released earlier today:

  • iOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24A5424a)
  • iPadOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24A5424a)
  • macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Beta 7 (Build: 26A5421a)
  • tvOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24J5358a)
  • visionOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24M5359a)
  • watchOS 27 Developer Beta 7 (Build: 24R5358a)

Apple is now releasing the corresponding versions for the public beta, marking the fifth round of public beta releases. As of now, Apple has released new public beta versions for iOS 27, tvOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, and HomePod 27.

Today's releases don't include any particularly notable changes, as Apple is now primarily focused on bug fixes and stability improvements ahead of the official launch, which is expected within the next few weeks.

In addition, Apple has also released the second release candidate (RC) of macOS Sequoia 15.8 (24H20), following this morning's release of the corresponding developer release candidate. The second release candidate of macOS Tahoe 26.7 (25G224) is also expected to be released soon. It has been available for download since 7:42 PM Eastern Time.

Across all of today's releases, the public beta build numbers match those of the corresponding developer betas.

Sign Up for Apple's Public Beta Program

If you'd like to enroll your device in the public beta program, visit https://beta.apple.com and follow the steps for your respective device. Here's how to install the public beta on iPhone:

  • Visit the Apple Beta Software Program website, then choose "Sign Up" or "Sign In."
  • Sign in with the same Apple Account you use on your iPhone. Then accept the program terms and enroll your account.
  • Open Settings on your iPhone.
  • Go to General > Software Update > Beta Updates.
  • Select "iOS 27 Public Beta."
  • Return to the Software Update screen, and tap "Update Now" when the beta appears.

Apple recommends installing beta software on a secondary device. If you're using your primary iPhone, be sure to back it up first.

Have you discovered any changes in today's beta? Let us know in the comments.
